sentences.en: Hello, everybody, and welcome back to The Psychology of Your 20s, the podcast where we talk through some of the big life changes
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到《你二十岁的心理学》，在这里我们探讨二十岁时遇到的一些重大生活改变

sentences.en: and transitions of our 20s and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 和过渡，以及它们对我们心理的意义。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody, welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到节目。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到本播客。

sentences.en: New listeners, old listeners, wherever you are in the world, it is so great to have you here back for another episode as we, of course, talk about the psychology of our 20s.
sentences.zh: 新听众、老听众，无论你身处世界的哪个角落，很高兴你能回来收听新的一期节目，当然，我们今天要聊聊二十岁的心理学。

sentences.en: Today, we are going to be talking about the psychology of revenge, what some of us might think of as an ugly feeling, but what is actually one of the most complex,
sentences.zh: 今天，我们要讨论的是复仇心理，有些人可能会认为这是一种丑陋的感觉，但它实际上是我们所能拥有的最复杂、

sentences.en: layered human emotions that we can have.
sentences.zh: 最有层次的人类情感之一。

sentences.en: Some of my absolute favorite movies and books are written about this concept.
sentences.zh: 我最喜欢的一些电影和书就是围绕这个概念创作的。

sentences.en: Think like Kill Bill or Promising Young Women or Taken, and I find our human need for, like, an eye for an eye so interesting.
sentences.zh: 比如《杀死比尔》、《前程似锦的女孩》或者《飓风营救》，我发现人类对以眼还眼这种事的诉求是如此有趣。

sentences.en: It's one of those universal human impulses that we all get, whether or not we've acted on it, whether or not we've acknowledged it or not.
sentences.zh: 这是我们所有人都会有的一种普遍人类冲动，无论我们是否付诸行动，无论我们是否承认它。

sentences.en: You know, if only I could make my ex hurt the way that they hurt me, if only I could get back at that friend who betrayed me or that person who cut me off on the road.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，要是我能让我前任受折磨，就像他们折磨我那样就好了，要是我能报复那个背叛我的朋友，或者路上把我超车别了一下的人就好了。

sentences.en: Sometimes it almost feels satisfying to either enact revenge or to daydream about all the ways we could.
sentences.zh: 有时候，去实施复仇或者空想各种复仇的方式，几乎会有一种满足感。

sentences.en: Is that a good thing?
sentences.zh: 这真的是件好事吗？

sentences.en: Why do we feel such, like, a weird pleasure around hurting someone who hurt us?
sentences.zh: 为什么伤害了我们的人遭受痛苦，我们会感到一种奇怪的快感？

sentences.en: Here's the paradox as well.
sentences.zh: 这里同样存在一个悖论。

sentences.en: Revenge promises satisfaction, but more often than not, you might not know this, you probably do, but it actually leaves us feeling emptier than before.
sentences.zh: 复仇承诺了满足感，但往往——你可能不知道，其实你大概也知道——它实际上让我们感到比以前更加空虚。

sentences.en: It might feel good initially.
sentences.zh: 它最初可能会让人觉得很爽。

sentences.en: Is it really worth the cost?
sentences.zh: 这真的值得付出代价吗？

sentences.en: And how do you navigate feeling such a messy, bitter feeling that maybe goes up against your more inherent desire to be a good person?
sentences.zh: 当你内心涌起这种混乱、苦涩的感觉，它或许与你想要做一个好人的固有愿望相冲突时，你该如何应对？

sentences.en: Why is the drive towards revenge so strong?
sentences.zh: 为什么复仇的驱动力会如此强烈？

sentences.en: When should we act on it?
sentences.zh: 我们什么时候应该付诸行动？

sentences.en: When should we avoid it?
sentences.zh: 我们什么时候应该避免这样做？

sentences.en: These are all the kind of questions that we're going to be answering today's episode, as well as looking at some listener stories of people who have sought revenge
sentences.zh: 这些都是我们今天这期节目要解答的问题，同时我们还会看看一些寻求过复仇的人的听众故事，

sentences.en: and what the consequences were.
sentences.zh: 以及随之而来的后果。

sentences.en: There is so much pettiness, so much drama in this episode, so many good stories, and also so much psychology.
sentences.zh: 这一期里有太多的抓马、太多的狗血剧情、那么多精彩的故事，还有那么多的心理学知识。

sentences.en: It's almost unbelievable.
sentences.zh: 简直让人难以置信。

sentences.en: So without further ado, let's get into the psychology of revenge.
sentences.zh: 废话不多说，让我们进入复仇心理学。

sentences.en: I feel like the idea of revenge is almost romantic at this point.
sentences.zh: 我觉得复仇这个概念在今天几乎带有一丝浪漫色彩。

sentences.en: It's like this driving force for so many dramatic moments.
sentences.zh: 它就像是无数戏剧性时刻的驱动力。

sentences.en: Some people would even call them poetic moments.
sentences.zh: 有些人甚至会称它们为充满诗意的时刻。

sentences.en: So what exactly is it about revenge that makes it so powerful and so hard to resist?
sentences.zh: 那么，复仇究竟有什么魔力，让它如此强大且让人难以抗拒？

sentences.en: To understand revenge, we really have to start at the origin feeling, at what is going on before we even decide to get back at someone.
sentences.zh: 要理解复仇，我们真的必须从最初的感受开始，看看在我们决定报复某人之前到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: When someone wrongs us, that's the beginning of this process, our brain obviously interprets it as a threat, not just to our safety, but also to more high-level cognitive values.
sentences.zh: 当有人对不起我们时，这是这个过程的开始，我们的大脑显然会将此解释为一个威胁，不仅是对我们安全的威胁，也是对更高层次认知价值观的威胁。

sentences.en: So things like social status.
sentences.zh: 比如社会地位。

sentences.en: It's a threat to social status.
sentences.zh: 这是对社会地位的威胁。

sentences.en: It's a threat to our sense of fairness.
sentences.zh: 这是对我们公平感的威胁。

sentences.en: It's also a threat to our identity.
sentences.zh: 这也是对我们身份认同的威胁。

sentences.en: Now, when you have a healthy ego, there is this like invisible protective boundary or shield around you.
sentences.zh: 现在，当你拥有一个健康的自我时，你的周围会有一道无形的保护边界或护盾。

sentences.en: It kind of represents like a limit of what you will and won't tolerate.
sentences.zh: 它某种程度上代表了你能够容忍和不能容忍的底线。

sentences.en: And when someone oversteps that boundary, when the shield is penetrated, that's when something pretty ancient in us is triggered.
sentences.zh: 而当有人跨越了那个边界，当护盾被击穿时，我们体内某个非常古老的东西就被触发了。

sentences.en: Now, some people's, you know, boundary shield is quite small and close to them, and some people's is quite wide.
sentences.zh: 现在，有些人的边界护盾相当小且贴近自己，而有些人的则相当宽广。

sentences.en: Regardless, it is actually completely subjective, but studies in the field of neuroscience have shown that when someone crosses that boundary,
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，这其实是完全主观的，但神经科学领域的研讨表明，当有人跨越了那个边界，

sentences.en: there is this specific area in our brain called the dorsal striatum that immediately lights up.
sentences.zh: 我们大脑中有一个被称为背侧纹状体的特定区域会立刻被点亮。

sentences.en: Interestingly, it's also the same area that lights up when we eat chocolate, when we win money, when we receive praise from somebody.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，当我们吃巧克力、赢得金钱、或者受到别人的赞扬时，被点亮的也是这个区域。

sentences.en: In other words, the anticipation of revenge after someone has hurt us, harmed us, betrayed us, literally does feel initially quite pleasurable.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，在经历伤害、遭到背叛后，对复仇的期待从最初开始确实会让人感到相当愉悦。

sentences.en: This, from an evolutionary perspective, makes a lot of sense.
sentences.zh: 从进化的角度来看，这非常合理。

sentences.en: We are wired to respond to injustice.
sentences.zh: 我们的基因注定了我们会对不公做出反应。

sentences.en: If we think about early groups of humans, we pretty much relied on this elusive concept of fairness to survive.
sentences.zh: 如果我们想想早期的人类群体，我们几乎完全依靠公平这个难以捉摸的概念来生存。

sentences.en: Being wronged, having your resources stolen, having your reputation undermined, having your partner taken,
sentences.zh: 受到不公对待、资源被盗、名誉受损、伴侣被抢，

sentences.en: that could and would threaten your survival.
sentences.zh: 这些都有可能而且确实会威胁到你的生存。

sentences.en: And so revenge served as a signal to others that this kind of behavior was unacceptable.
sentences.zh: 因此，复仇向其他人发出了一种信号，表明这种行为是不可接受的。

sentences.en: So in a way, it actually worked to reinforce social rules and to deter people or others from betrayal or from hurting people.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种程度上说，它实际上起到了强化社会规则、阻止他人背叛或伤害别人的作用。

sentences.en: Basically, it's like the classic idea of punishment, punishing the offender, teaching them a lesson, restoring harmony, and also signaling to the wider group that this is not okay,
sentences.zh: 基本上，这就像惩罚的经典理念，惩罚违规者、给他们一个教训、恢复和谐，同时也向更广泛的群体发出信号，表明这种事是不行的，

sentences.en: but also that you are not an easy target.
sentences.zh: 并且也表明你不是一个容易捏的软柿子。

sentences.en: And this kind of reputational enforcement that you are not somebody to be messed with was really adaptive in smaller communities where reputation affected access to mates,
sentences.zh: 这种名誉上的维护——即你不是一个可以招惹的人——在较小的社区中具有极高的适应性，因为在这些地方，名誉会影响你获取伴侣、

sentences.en: to protection, to resources.
sentences.zh: 获得保护和资源的途径。

sentences.en: So long before laws or social contracts, this instinct was really, really helpful.
sentences.zh: 因此，早在法律或社会契约出现之前，这种本能就非常非常有用了。

sentences.en: It's actually what psychologists would call altruistic punishment.
sentences.zh: 这其实就是心理学家所说的利他性惩罚。

sentences.en: Basically, yes, the outcome of revenge might not be necessarily positive for the other person, but it also has a greater good in that it used to maintain group cooperation
sentences.zh: 基本上，是的，复仇的结果对另一个人来说可能不一定是积极的，但它也有更大的益处，即它过去被用来维护群体的合作，

sentences.en: and it actually used to be good for social harmony, knowing that there was this balance between giving people respect and knowing that if you overstepped your boundary,
sentences.zh: 而且它实际上曾有利于社会和谐，因为人们知道在给予他人尊重与跨越边界之间存在着这样一种平衡，

sentences.en: you would also receive some kind of punishment that taught you not to do that.
sentences.zh: 如果你越界了，你也会受到某种惩罚，从而吸取教训不再这样做。

sentences.en: So it is a very, very old feeling.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种非常非常古老的感觉。

sentences.en: That's what we need to understand, especially if you feel a lot of guilt around wanting to enact revenge against someone.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们需要理解的，尤其是当你对想要报复某人感到内心充满负罪感时。

sentences.en: The question that we kind of get into is why would it therefore still be useful in modern life?
sentences.zh: 我们接下来要探讨的问题是，为什么它在现代生活中居然仍然有用？

sentences.en: You know, when we have laws and law enforcement, when we have rules, when we have a legal system, why do we still feel the feeling if technically there are other systems
sentences.zh: 你知道的，当我们拥有法律和执法机构、拥有规则、拥有法律体系时，为什么我们仍然会有这种感觉，如果从技术上讲有其他系统

sentences.en: that are meant to, you know, take care of that for us?
sentences.zh: 本来应该替我们处理好这些事情的话？

sentences.en: The most obvious driver for revenge is this need for justice.
sentences.zh: 复仇最明显的驱动力是对正义的需求。

sentences.en: And I know I just mentioned the legal system and law enforcement system.
sentences.zh: 我知道我刚才提到了法律体系和执法系统。

sentences.en: What if that system is broken?
sentences.zh: 但如果那个系统是崩溃的呢？

sentences.en: What if that system doesn't work in your interests?
sentences.zh: 如果那个系统不符合你的利益呢？

sentences.en: What if the thing that someone did wasn't necessarily illegal,
sentences.zh: 如果某人做的事情不一定违法，

sentences.en: but still really hurt you deeply?
sentences.zh: 但仍然深深地伤害了你呢？

sentences.en: Like, what if they, what if it was someone who cheated or something really petty and small that you couldn't necessarily sue someone for,
sentences.zh: 比如，如果是一个人出轨了，或者是一些你无法对别人提起诉讼的极度琐碎的小事，

sentences.en: but which still really annoyed you and hurt you?
sentences.zh: 但却仍然真的惹恼了你、伤害了你呢？

sentences.en: I remember when my ex was secretly dating someone whilst we were having like discussions of like, do we get back together or not?
sentences.zh: 我还记得我的前任在我们正讨论着“我们要不要复合”的时候，偷偷和别人约会。

sentences.en: And we were having all these talks about like, no, we definitely have a future together.
sentences.zh: 当时我们一直在谈论诸如“不，我们俩绝对有未来”之类的话。

sentences.en: Give me a second chance.
sentences.zh: “再给我一次机会。”

sentences.en: And the whole time he was dating somebody else.
sentences.zh: 然而整个过程中他都在和别人约会。

sentences.en: And when I found out, I had never felt that surge of adrenaline before.
sentences.zh: 当我发现的时候，我从未体验过那种汹涌的肾上腺素飙升。

sentences.en: That like, this, to be honest, like desire to hurt him.
sentences.zh: 坦白讲，那种想要伤害他的欲望。

sentences.en: And it honestly, like, it shocked me.
sentences.zh: 老实说，这让我感到震惊。

sentences.en: Like it made me see myself differently as an individual.
sentences.zh: 这让我以一种不同的眼光看待自己作为个体的形象。

sentences.en: This is like the classic, they must pay kind of motive.
sentences.zh: 这就是典型的“他们必须付出代价”的动机。

sentences.en: The belief that for fairness to be enacted,
sentences.zh: 坚信要实现公平，

sentences.en: retribution is somewhat required.
sentences.zh: 报应在某种程度上是必需的。

sentences.en: Revenge also allows us to reassert control.
sentences.zh: 复仇也让我们能够重新掌控主动权。

sentences.en: If we've been betrayed, humiliated, or made to feel powerless,
sentences.zh: 如果我们遭到背叛、羞辱，或者被搞得觉得自己无能为力，

sentences.en: like fantasizing about payback gives us a sense of agency, even if we don't do anything about it.
sentences.zh: 那么幻想报复就会给我们一种掌控感，即使我们什么都没做。

sentences.en: There's this idea of like, yes, this person stepped all over me.
sentences.zh: 这就好比这种想法：是的，这个人把我踩在脚下。

sentences.en: Yes, this person hurt me.
sentences.zh: 是的，这个人伤害了我。

sentences.en: But I know I could get back at them if I wanted to.
sentences.zh: 但我知道如果我想的话，我可以报复他们。

sentences.en: And therefore, I actually do have some level of control in this situation.
sentences.zh: 因此，在这种情况下我实际上确实拥有某种程度的控制力。

sentences.en: So it kind of serves as this like emotional, moral, like psychological recalibration that stops us from being additionally hurt by this idea that we are powerless
sentences.zh: 所以它在某种程度上起到了情感、道德和心理上的重新校准作用，阻止我们因为觉得自己对别人对我们做的事无能为力

sentences.en: to what people do to us.
sentences.zh: 而遭受进一步的伤害。

sentences.en: Many people also believe that revenge actually helps people get closure.
sentences.zh: 许多人还相信复仇实际上能帮助人们获得释怀。

sentences.en: There's this perception that if you retaliate and make someone feel the way that they made you feel, that is when you can walk away.
sentences.zh: 人们有一种看法，如果你进行报复并让别人感受到他们让你感受到的痛苦，那就是你能抽身离开的时候。
